To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Andreev reflections at normal conductor-sruperconductor interfaces of Sr2RuO3 can be used to distinguish different superconducting phases.
(a) Andreev reflection is sensitive to spin triplet superconducting order, (b) the Andreev conductance peak is related to the existence of surface bound states in a superconductor.
Andreev reflections at interfaces between normal conductors and superconductors in triplet states are strongly angle-dependent.

the study of the electronic structure of materials, in particular the electronic structure of the high temperature superconductor YBCO, the heavy-fermion superconductor CeCu2Si2 and the unconventional superconductor Sr2RuO3.

the physics of the superconductor-insulator transition in two dimensions, with the physics of superconductivity at the edge and in the bulk of a two dimensional electron gas, and with the physics of unconventional superconductors.
the study of the electronic and magnetic properties of novel superconducting materials, and their potential applications in spintronics, quantum computing and nanotechnology.

the experimental results are consistent with a triplet pairing state, but cannot be used to distinguish between the various possibilities.

the Andreev conductance peaks in the normal conductor are a characteristic fingerprint of the superconducting state in the superconduc-tor and thus can be used to determine the symmetry of the pairing.
the superconducting state in Sr2RuO(4) has a non-unitary triplet pairing symmetry with an equal mixture of the two spin-triplet channels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can distinguish between unitary and non-unitary triplet pairing states in Sr2RuO3.
we have shown that the Andreev reflections of the quasiparticles in the normal metal are sensitive to the symmetry of the superconducting pairing state.
we have studied the Andreev reflections of a normal metal-superconductor interface in the case of a triplet pairing state, which is a non-unitary state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Andreev-reflection properties are sensitive to the symmetry of the superconducting order parameter.
the quasiparticles in Sr2RuO$_4$ can be used as a probe of the superconducting pairing state in this system.
